reasoning: The package contains only standard AUR packaging files: a PKGBUILD that downloads verified binaries from the official Technitium domain with proper checksums, a systemd service file with justified capabilities for a DNS server, and a sysusers.d declaration for creating a dedicated service user. No malicious code, no execution of fetched content, no unexpected network requests. The 'inconclusive' result from qwen3-235b was caused by an API error (HTTP 400) when auditing the sysuser file, not by any security concern. The deepseek model successfully audited the same file and correctly identified it as a benign systemd-sysusers declaration. The advisory report from openrouter/free corroborates this assessment.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from a tool error in the qwen3-235b model, which failed to audit technitium-dns-server.sysuser due to an HTTP 400 BadRequestError. This caused the model to return 'inconclusive' for the entire package. The deepseek model successfully reviewed the same file and found it safe, which is the correct assessment for a standard sysusers.d configuration file. The openrouter/free report (advisory only) also found all files safe. There is no substantive security disagreement; the inconclusive result is purely a tool failure.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to audit technitium-dns-server.sysuser due to API error (HTTP 400), resulting in incomplete coverage
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should not propagate to package-level 'inconclusive' verdicts when the failed file is trivially safe and other models have successfully audited it
The audit tool should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool error' and 'inconclusive due to genuine security uncertainty' in its final verdict logic
For simple configuration files like sysusers.d declarations, consider implementing a fast-path assessment or fallback mechanism to avoid tool errors on trivially safe content
When multiple models are used, a tool error in one model should not override successful audits from other models on the same files
